---
title: Command line and URLs
description: "Every command and flag, and the URL parameters that hand a study to the browser runner."
---

| Command | Arguments | Useful flags | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `convert` | `<input> <output>` | `--into <png>` | Rewrites a studyflow between the YAML spelling, BPMN XML, and `.studyflow.png`; the output extension picks the format. |
| `validate` | `<input>` | `--strict` | Reads the file and prints warnings and errors; exits non-zero on errors, or on warnings too with `--strict`. |
| `info` | `<input>` | `--json` | Prints the study's id, name, version, what kind of file it came from, and how many of each element it holds. |
| `run` | `<input> [runnerArgs...]` | `--runtime <name>` | Runs the study where it says it should run; everything after the input file is passed on to the runner. |
| `render` | `[names...]` | `--dir <dir>`, `--origin <origin>` | Re-draws the example `.studyflow.png` images. Only works inside a clone of the repository. |

Different programs take their arguments differently. The CLI and the Python runner take a command line. The browser runner takes its arguments in the address bar. The modeler takes none.

Every command answers `--help`, and `studyflow --version` prints the version.

## Installing

The CLI is one file with nothing under it --- no Node.js, no interpreter, no packages to install alongside.

```bash
brew tap morteza/studyflow https://github.com/morteza/studyflow-modeler
brew install studyflow
```

macOS and Linux, on Apple silicon, ARM and Intel. Anywhere else, or to run the tip of the tree, build it in a checkout of the repository, where it runs under Node.js instead:

```bash
npm install
npm run build -w @behaverse/studyflow-cli
```

## Companions

A subcommand this CLI does not answer to is looked up on your PATH, the way `git lfs` finds `git-lfs`: `studyflow xyz` runs `studyflow-xyz`, passes the rest of the command line to it untouched, and exits with whatever it exited with. `studyflow --help` lists the companions you have installed.

That is how the parts of the toolchain that are not one binary arrive. The Python runner is the first of them: `uv tool install studyflow-runner` puts `studyflow-run` on your PATH, and `studyflow run` uses it.

## Where `run` sends a study

`studyflow run` reads the `runtime` that the study declares. That value is `cloud` unless you set it to something else. Passing `--runtime` overrides it for a single invocation.

| Declared runtime | What the CLI does |
|---|---|
| `local` | Hands the study to the Python runner, passing your trailing arguments through. |
| `browser` | Stops with instructions instead: a study that participants sit through belongs in the browser runner, at `<site>/run/`. |
| `cloud` | Stops with an error --- nothing is wired up for it. `--runtime local` runs the study on this machine instead. |
| `hpc` | Same as `cloud`. |
| anything else | Refused, with the four listed. |

A YAML input is converted to a temporary `.bpmn` file first: BPMN XML, on its own or embedded in a PNG, is what the Python runner reads.

## The Python runner

One script, declaring its own dependencies, so this needs nothing installed beforehand.

```bash
cd packages/runner-py
uv run studyflow_run.py ../../assets/examples/sklearn_pipeline.studyflow.png
uv run --with torch studyflow_run.py my_pipeline.studyflow.png   # software your study names
```

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--repo <DIR>` | The run repository to write into; its name becomes the run id. Defaults to the study's own directory when the study already lives in one, otherwise a fresh `runs/<UTC start time>`. |
| `--from <REF>` | Re-run from a point in that repository's history, branching there. |
| `--fresh` | Ignore the records of what has already run, and run every step again. |
| `--no-prepare-inputs` | Fail on a missing input at the edge of the study rather than fall back to a shipped example's own. |
| `--quiet` | No console output. The log file is written either way. |

There is no seed flag: the root seed is the one pinned on the study, or one drawn per run and recorded on the archived copy that run leaves behind.

| `studyflow run` looks for the runner | In this order |
|---|---|
| the `STUDYFLOW_RUN_PY` environment variable | first |
| `studyflow-run` on your PATH, the installed companion | second |
| the copy that ships beside the CLI, with `uv` on your PATH | third |

The middle one is the ordinary route: `uv tool install studyflow-runner`, once. The copy that ships beside the CLI is the fallback that needs no install at all, and there `uv` fetches the study's dependencies on each run rather than up front.

## The browser runner's URL parameters

The browser runner is served at `/run/`. One parameter says what to run; every other one binds a value into the study.

| Parameter | Value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `diagram` | the name of a shipped demo (`behaverse`) | Runs that demo studyflow. |
| `diagram` | a URL --- anything with a scheme, a slash, or a studyflow file extension | Fetched, then run. |
| `diagram` | a hand-off id (a bare 8-character slice of a uuid) | Runs the studyflow the modeler just handed over; the hand-off expires after an hour. |
| `seed` | an integer | Binds to the study's `seed`, fixing the random draws so the same participant path can be replayed. |
| any other name | text, converted to the declared type | Binds to a `Parameters` entry, a `bpmn:Property`, or a field of the study, and is substituted wherever `${name}` is written. A name the study declares nowhere is still bound, and logged as undeclared. |
| nothing | a `${name}` in the study that no parameter binds | Stops the run with an error naming it. |

```
run?diagram=URL&seed=42
run?diagram=behaverse&task=BCS&timeline=XCIT_BCS_02
```

[Run with participants](../run/participants.qmd) walks through one.

## What `render` needs

`render` re-draws each image by opening the modeler in a browser, loading the example, and exporting it.

It defaults to `--dir assets/examples` and `--origin http://127.0.0.1:4175`. If nothing is listening at that origin, it starts the modeler's dev server itself.

```bash
npx playwright install chromium   # once per machine
```

| It also needs | Or else |
|---|---|
| the browser that command downloads | `render` stops --- without Playwright itself, telling you to run `npm run examples:render` from inside the repository; without the browser, with Playwright's own message |
| a connection, for the icons | every image is written without its element icons, and the warning that says so is raised inside the browser `render` drives, not in your terminal. Look at the images before keeping them. |

| Then read | For |
|---|---|
| [File format](file-format.qmd) | the formats `convert` moves a study between |
| [Execution](../run/execution.qmd) | what a program does with the study once it is handed one |
| [Run with participants](../run/participants.qmd) | a session from the participant's side |
